text:
maya: Heads-up — we've been seeing higher variance in KV residency on long chats, eviction spikes after ~10k tokens :thinking_face:
liam: same, hit rate drops from ~98% to ~82% on a few busy hosts :eyes:
maya: quick PromQL I used to spot the spikes:
```
sum(increase(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (host)
```
liam: also useful: sliding hit-rate by model:
```
( increase(kv_hit_count[5m]) / (increase(kv_hit_count[5m]) + increase(kv_miss_count[5m])) )
```
arjun: can we break that by model + seq_len_bucket? I suspect long-context model variants suffer more
nina: +1, a per-model heatmap for residency would help triage
sofia: propose alert proto: `WHEN increase(kv_evictions_total[10m]) > 30 AND kv_hit_rate < 0.9 FOR 5m` -> page on-call
dev-bot: runtime/canary deploy v2.3.1 finished at 1987655200
maya: that canary included a kernel-selector tweak and a change to batching heuristics; may be related
liam: profiler shows more work in the cache lookup path, likely due to fragmentation causing longer walks, sample traces: trace_id=tr-0a1b2c
arjun: suggested dashboard panels:
- residency heatmap (seq_len_bucket x host)
- eviction rate by age (evictions per bucket)
- reuse ratio = evicted_but_reused / evictions_total
- sliding hit-rate per model
- sampler panel: fraction of fragments > threshold
nina: I can mock these in Grafana if someone lists canonical metric names + labels
maya: metric list to expose/confirm:
- kv_hit_count
- kv_miss_count
- kv_residency_bytes (gauge)
- kv_residency_bytes_bucket (histogram)
- kv_fragments_total
- kv_fragmentation_ratio (derived metric)
- kv_evictions_total
- kv_reuse_hits
sofia: add tags: `model`, `seq_len_bucket`, `host`, `pool_type` (dedicated vs hosted) for routing visibility
maya: runbook sketch for alert:
1) check eviction spike panel + host
2) run `kv-stats sample --host HOST` to get fragment distribution
3) if fragmentation high -> temporarily pin to older kernel-selector or increase compactness threshold
4) if hit_rate still low -> drain host from pool and escalate to eng-runtime
liam: also add a perf regression test in CI that runs long-context workload for 30s and asserts hit_rate > 0.95
nina: I'll create a dashboard PR and add the alert rule + runbook doc, assigning to eng-runtime on the PR
maya: thanks everyone :+1: let's sync tomorrow in the standup if PR isn't ready
sofia: noted, added to my TODOs :spiral_notepad:
liam: small note — we should instrument `kv_lookup_steps` (histogram of steps per lookup) to track fragmentation impact
arjun: agreed, that + reuse ratio should make root-cause much faster
maya: ok locking this thread for action items: Nina -> dashboard + alert, Liam -> perf test, Sofia -> labels/metrics, Arjun -> collector changes
nina: taking it, will ping when PR is up :rocket:
